## What's new in 1.6.1

**Beavis and Butt-head Screen Wreckers: twenty-four releases, 479 modules.**

| Release | Year | Modules |
|---|---|---|
| Beavis and Butt-head Screen Wreckers | 1996 | 9 |

Viacom New Media's Screen Wreckers, one of MTV's "Cheap Clicks", made by Cyclops Software as a set of its Desktop Toys: nine toys in which Beavis and Butt-head wreck your desktop. Beavis eats the sweets and caffeine that fly in while the Cornholio meter fills (Cornholio); the two tumble about in a tractor tire and drag skid marks through your windows (Tire Trouble); Beavis punches and kicks the TVs, pots and nachos hurled at him (Karate Beavis); they spray-paint graffiti over the screen (Painting Dudes), kick a trash can until its garbage piles up (Kick The Can), throw slurpies, eggs and milk at it (Chuckfest), spray it with shaken sodas (Soda Jerks), shoot the targets flying across it (Shoot 'Em) and mow it into stripes (Digger).

Its screen saver played a toy in "ghost mode", the toy playing itself over your desktop, and that is how Long After Dark plays each of them, over a picture of your desktop, at the pace they had on Windows 95. **Caps Lock makes the toy yours to play**, with its own controls: the mouse in most of them (a right click changes the paint, the object or the weapon; F2 switches between Beavis and Butt-head), the arrow keys and Space in Tire Trouble and Digger, and the keypad in Karate Beavis, with Num Lock on. Esc twice, Ctrl+Q or EXIT ends your game and the toy plays itself again, as does Caps Lock off. In the living wallpaper (`LongAfterDark.exe /wallpaper`) the toys wreck a picture of your wallpaper.

It is the set's own Windows 95 program, which Long After Dark runs unchanged: the first 32-bit program it runs whole, started as the set's screen saver started it.

**Importing it.** The importer takes it from your CD, a folder copied from it, or its ISO image, which it can download from the Internet Archive (46.1 MB). It reads the CD's InstallShield 3 archives and installs only the toys' program and files, and checks every one of them against the original disc.

**Twenty-four covers.** The importer's window shows them eight to a row.
